page.title: Agent mode
page.purpose: Give a goal to an agent, watch it act under explicit bounds, and promote a successful run into a deterministic flow.

priorities.statement: Step, cost, and lease bounds are visible before the run starts and counted down during it.
priorities.notes: An unbounded agent on a personal device is the failure mode this surface exists to prevent.

priorities.statement: Abort is available at every moment of the run.
priorities.notes: Bounds handle the expected case; abort handles the rest.

priorities.statement: A successful run offers promotion into a flow with the AI steps resolved away.
priorities.notes: Infer once, replay free — the promotion path is the reason agent mode earns its cost.

states.description: A device is selected and a goal can be entered under stated bounds.
Agent runtime availability and lease state are being resolved.
No agent run has been performed on this device; the goal entry and its bounds are the whole page.
The run reached its goal partially — some recorded steps succeeded and the goal was not confirmed. Promotion is not offered.
A prior run's transcript is shown after the device's capability snapshot changed, so its steps may no longer be executable.
The agent runtime call failed mid-run; the partial step record is retained and the failure is stated.
No agent run in progress; goal entry available.
Run active with remaining step and cost budget displayed.
A bound was reached; the run stopped and says which bound.
Operator cancelled; partial step record retained.
Goal reached; promotion to a deterministic flow offered.
agent-manager or the operator skill is unreachable; the missing dependency is named.

elements.name: Goal
elements.description: The natural-language goal handed to the agent runtime.

elements.name: Bounds
elements.description: Step ceiling, cost ceiling, and lease duration — set before the run and enforced during it.
Live countdown of remaining steps, remaining cost budget, and lease time.

elements.name: Abort
elements.description: Stops the run immediately, retaining the partial step record.

elements.name: Steps
elements.description: Each agent action recorded as a flow step, which is what makes promotion possible.
Names which bound stopped the run, distinguishing exhaustion from failure.

elements.name: Promote to flow
elements.description: Exports the recorded steps as a deterministic flow that replays without inference cost.

elements.name: Lease held
elements.description: The global lease alarm. An agent run always holds a lease for its duration.
Names which dependency — the agent runtime or the operator skill — is unreachable.

claims.statement: Step, cost, and lease bounds are perceivable before a run can be started.
claims.rationale: Priority 1. An unbounded agent holding a lease on a personal phone is the failure this surface exists to prevent, and bounds set after the fact are not bounds.

claims.statement: Remaining step, cost, and lease budget are perceivable throughout an active run.
claims.rationale: Priority 1. A bound the operator cannot watch approaching gives no opportunity to intervene early.

claims.statement: Abort is reachable without scrolling at every moment of an active run.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. Bounds handle the expected case; abort handles the rest, and it must not require hunting.

claims.statement: Abort is operable from the keyboard during an active run.
claims.rationale: Consistent with the kill control: a safety affordance that needs a pointer is not always available.

claims.statement: A run stopped by a bound states which bound stopped it.
claims.rationale: 'Stopped' without a cause is indistinguishable from a crash, and the remedy differs per bound.

claims.statement: A run that exhausted a bound is perceivably different from one the operator aborted.
claims.rationale: One says the task was larger than its budget; the other says a human intervened. They lead to different next actions.

claims.statement: A successful run offers promotion into a deterministic flow.
claims.rationale: Priority 3 and OT-P1-006. Promotion is the compounding loop that justifies agent mode's cost; if it is not offered at the moment of success it will not be discovered.

claims.statement: Promotion is not offered for a run that did not reach its goal.
claims.rationale: Promoting an unproven sequence would mint a deterministic flow that never worked, which is worse than no flow.

claims.statement: The recorded step transcript remains readable after abort, exhaustion, and runtime failure.
claims.rationale: The transcript is both the audit record and the promotion source; discarding it on an unhappy path destroys both.

claims.statement: When agent mode cannot start, the unreachable dependency is named rather than reported generically.
claims.rationale: INTEGRATIONS.md commits to agent mode refusing rather than improvising without the skill; the refusal must say which of the two is missing.
